main_zone_off.description: Turn the main zone off (ASCII ZM), leaving the unit powered.

main_zone_on.description: Turn the main zone on (ASCII ZM), leaving the unit itself powered. On the single-zone AVR-S720W this is indistinguishable from power_on; it is declared because the distinction is real on multi-zone siblings covered by the same surface.

mute_on.description: Mute the main zone. Reads back as lower-case `on` in the status documents.

power_on.description: Bring the whole unit out of standby. Requires Network Control = Always On; with it off nothing on the LAN can wake the receiver.
power_on.example_notes: The DIRECT-route equivalent is `GET /goform/formiPhoneAppDirect.xml?PWON`; both are accepted and neither reports failure in its response. Allow a second or two before polling — the receiver's HTTP server is unresponsive while it powers up, and a read issued immediately can time out even though the command took.

power_standby.description: Put the whole unit into standby.

query_status.description: Read the main-zone state. Not a control command — declared so entities have a named state read, exactly as their writes have named commands.

returns.description: Signed dB decimal, or `--` at minimum.
returns.name: MasterVolume.value

select_input.description: Select an input source by its wire token. Send only tokens the unit itself listed in `<InputFuncList>`; an unlisted one is accepted with a 200 and silently does nothing.

source.description: Input wire token without the SI prefix: MPLAY, SAT/CBL, BD, DVD, GAME, TV, AUX1, TUNER, NET, BT.
source.notes: `SAT/CBL` contains a slash, which is legal unencoded in a query string; encode it as %2F only if your HTTP client insists.

select_surround_mode.description: Request a surround mode. The receiver may substitute a different one based on what the incoming stream actually is, and reports the substitution rather than an error — re-read `<SurrMode>` afterwards.

mode.description: Mode name without the MS prefix, RAW and unencoded: MOVIE, MUSIC, GAME, DIRECT, PURE DIRECT, STEREO, AUTO, MCH STEREO, VIRTUAL.
mode.notes: Raw because the same token is what `<SurrMode>` reports back, so one spelling serves both the send and the state match. The renderer percent-encodes the space as it builds the request line — see `protocol_details.denon_common.request_format.escaping`. Substituting a value that is already encoded gives `MSMCH%2520STEREO`; substituting a raw one without encoding puts a bare space in the request line and the receiver drops the request.

set_sleep_timer.description: Set the sleep timer in minutes, or turn it off.

minutes.description: Three zero-padded digits, 010-120, or the literal `OFF`.

set_volume_db.description: Set the main-zone volume to an absolute level in dB — the same units the status documents report, so a client can round-trip a reading without converting.

volume_db.description: Signed decimal dB relative to reference, one decimal place, half-dB resolution: `-40.0`, `-39.5`. Send it with the decimal point — the bare integer form belongs to the ASCII MV command, not to this endpoint.
volume_db.notes: The upper end is what the hardware accepts, not what is safe. The receiver enforces its own configured ceiling, `MVMAX`, and clamps anything above it. That ceiling is NOT readable over HTTP: `MV?` answers on the ASCII channel, so only a port 23 client can read it, and no goform status document carries it. A consumer restricted to HTTP therefore cannot know the real maximum — it should treat +18 as the protocol bound rather than a promise, and expect a set above the ceiling to come back clamped in the next status read rather than as an error.

set_volume_offset.description: The same setting over the DIRECT route, in the ASCII command's OFFSET units — `MV50` is -30 dB, because 80 is the 0 dB reference. Declared so the conversion is written down somewhere executable; `set_volume_db` is the one to bind a control to.

offset.description: Two digits, or three when the level lands on a half step. Whole steps are `00`-`98` with `80` at 0 dB; a half step appends a `5` to the zero-padded two-digit whole part, so -29.5 dB is `505` and -75.5 dB is `045`.
offset.notes:
Build it from an integer count of half-steps, not by formatting a fractional number:

  n     = round((dB + 80) * 2)      # 0..196
  whole = n // 2                    # 0..98
  half  = n % 2                     # 0 or 1
  text  = f"{whole:02d}" + ("5" if half else "")

The zero-padding is load-bearing and the two-digit width is what makes the third digit unambiguous. Formatting `n / 2` and stripping the decimal point instead produces `45` for -75.5 dB, which the receiver reads as the whole step 45 — -35 dB, and 40 dB louder than asked for.

volume_down.description: Step the main-zone volume down by the receiver's own increment.

volume_up.description: Step the main-zone volume up by the receiver's own increment.

identity.notes:
The default hostname is model-derived — `Denon-AVR-S720W.local` on the observed unit — so it identifies the model but not the unit, and it changes if the owner renames the receiver. Use the UDN (SSDP) or the AirPlay `deviceid` (mDNS) as the stable key.
Among the mDNS records only `_airplay._tcp`'s `deviceid` is a true per-unit key. The `_http._tcp` hostname, the `_raop._tcp` instance name and the `_spotify-connect._tcp` instance name are unique on a link (DNS-SD guarantees that much, so they will not collide in a scan) but they all change when the owner renames the receiver — they keep entries apart, they do not survive a rename.
Whether the UDN's MAC and the AirPlay `deviceid` are the SAME address was not established here: the contributed scan redacted both below the 00:05:CD OUI before it reached this file, and a receiver with both Ethernet and Wi-Fi has two MACs. So treat each key as stable WITHIN its transport, and join an SSDP hit to an mDNS hit by IP address rather than by assuming the two identifiers match.

parse_rules:
Take the description URL verbatim from the LOCATION header and use it for UPnP only. Do not carry its port over to the control surface: goform is always on port 80, whatever port LOCATION names. (The observed scan recorded the services and the SERVER header but not the LOCATION line itself, so this spec states no port for the description document — resolving it from the header is the rule precisely because we cannot name it.)
The description is standard UPnP with the urn:schemas-upnp-org:device-1-0 namespace; match element local names, not prefixed ones.
IDENTIFICATION WITHOUT FETCHING: the M-SEARCH reply's SERVER header on this generation reads `KnOS/3.2 UPnP/1.0 DMP/3.5`. A SERVER value containing `KnOS/` is a D&M firmware platform and nothing else uses it, so it promotes a generic MediaRenderer hit to a positive vendor identification before any HTTP request.
The USN/UDN node field is the device's MAC: `uuid:XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-0005CDAABBCC`. A UDN whose last twelve hex digits begin `0005cd` is a D&M device, so those digits are a second vendor signal available without an HTTP fetch — and the UDN as a whole is this device's stable identity. They are NOT a join key against the AirPlay `deviceid`: a receiver has a wired and a wireless MAC and the two records may carry different ones. Join an SSDP hit to an mDNS hit by address; see `identity.notes`.

txt_match.description: The AirPlay device id is the unit's MAC, colon-separated, and 00:05:CD is IEEE-registered to D&M Holdings — observed on the live unit. Family-wide, like `identification.mac_prefixes`: it says "a D&M device", and the `model` record then names which one. Case-insensitive because hex case here is the mDNS stack's formatting choice, not a fact about the device.

`am` is the RAOP model record — `AVRS720W` on the observed unit. The prefix narrows the platform type to a Denon AVR receiver rather than to this model, deliberately: the family shares the surface (AVR-S920W, AVR-X1300W, and siblings this project has no evidence for), and the exact model is read from the record's full value. Weaker than the `deviceid` and `cpath` conditions on the sibling methods — prefer those where both were seen.
D&M's own web-API namespace inside Spotify's TXT record — observed verbatim on the live unit, constant across the D&M catalogue. Identifies the family; never the unit.

mac_prefixes.notes: IEEE assigns 00:05:CD to D&M Holdings — the block genuinely belongs to the manufacturer, but it covers the whole Denon and Marantz catalogue (receivers, network players, Heos speakers), so a match means "a D&M device", never "an AVR-S720W". Observed on the live unit in both the AirPlay `deviceid` TXT record and the node field of the SSDP UDN.

mdns_txt_match.description: Spotify's zeroconf TXT record names the config path the device serves, and on D&M firmware that path lives under `/goform/` — the vendor's own web-API namespace, which no other maker uses. Observed verbatim on the live unit. Constant across the whole D&M catalogue, so it identifies the family, never the unit — identity comes from the SSDP UDN or the AirPlay `deviceid`, not from this record.

device.name: Denon AVR-S720W AV Receiver
device.notes: Local control of a Denon AVR-S720W needs no account, no pairing and no token: anything that can route to the receiver can drive it. Two interchangeable command routes carry the same ASCII vocabulary — HTTP GET `/goform/formiPhoneAppDirect.xml?<CMD>` on port 80, and a raw TCP session on port 23 — plus a set of purpose-built goform form endpoints for power, volume and mute, and XML status documents for reading state back. State reads are polled: `/goform/formMainZone_MainZoneXmlStatusLite.xml` is the cheap one (power, input, volume, mute), the non-Lite document adds the per-unit input list, renamed sources and surround mode. Port 23 accepts ONE connection at a time and pushes unsolicited state changes; a consumer that holds it locks every other client (including the vendor app) out, so prefer polling over HTTP unless push is genuinely needed. Everything on the LAN goes dark in standby unless Setup > Network > Network Control is set to "Always On"; with it off, no LAN request — and no Wake-on-LAN path documented for this generation — can bring the unit up. Discovery is generic on its face (mDNS `_http._tcp`, `_airplay._tcp`, `_raop._tcp`, `_spotify-connect._tcp`; SSDP `MediaRenderer:1`), so identification leans on three vendor-shaped details instead: the `KnOS/` SERVER string, the Spotify Connect `cpath` of `/goform/spotifyConfig` (the `/goform/` prefix is D&M's own namespace), and the D&M `00:05:CD` OUI that appears both in the AirPlay `deviceid` and as the node field of the SSDP UDN.

openness.notes: Denon publishes a control-protocol document per receiver, which is why this is `documented_api` rather than `undocumented` — but the published document covers the ASCII command vocabulary only. The HTTP transport that carries it, the `/goform/` status documents every client actually polls, and the `AppCommand.xml` envelope are nowhere in it; those were recovered by the community, which is why `reverse_engineered` is true.

credentials.notes: There is no authentication anywhere on the local control surface: no pairing, no PIN, no token, no session. Anything that can route to port 80 or port 23 has full control of the receiver — it can power it on at 3 a.m. at whatever volume it likes — so network reachability IS the access-control model, and a consumer should say so rather than imply a credential protects it. The Wi-Fi passphrase is typed on the receiver (or copied over USB from an iOS device), so it never crosses a link a client of this spec implements.
stored_on_device: Spotify Connect user blob, once a Spotify client has added a user
Input renames, speaker calibration and menu settings

factory_reset.description: Denon documents two different operations and they are not interchangeable. "Reset network settings" (Setup > Network > Reset) clears only the network configuration and is what a user wants when moving to a new router — the front-panel procedure below is the full microprocessor reset and throws away the Audyssey calibration too, which is an hour of somebody's afternoon with a measurement microphone. Neither procedure has been performed by this project, and the front-panel button pair varies across the S-series and across model years, so confirm it against the unit's own manual before telling a user to hold anything.
factory_reset.effect: Clears network settings, input renames, speaker/Audyssey calibration and every menu setting; the receiver returns to its out-of-box state and re-runs the setup assistant.

procedures.basis: Denon's S-series setup-menu structure as described in the AVR-S720W owner's manual; not performed here.
procedures.name: Reset network settings only (menu)

steps.action: Setup > Network > Reset (some model years: 'Restore Defaults' inside the Network menu).
steps.expect: Network settings return to defaults; other settings and the Audyssey calibration survive.

procedures.basis: The Denon S-series "Resetting factory settings" convention — power off, then hold the two TUNER PRESET CH buttons while pressing the power button until the display flashes. Recorded because it is the first thing to try on a receiver whose menu is unreachable; the exact button pair differs by model year and this project has not run it.
procedures.indicator: The front-panel display flashes at roughly one-second intervals.
procedures.name: Full microprocessor reset (front panel)

steps.action: Put the receiver into standby with the front-panel power button.
Press and hold TUNER PRESET CH + and TUNER PRESET CH − together, then press the power button.
Release both buttons once the display begins flashing.
steps.expect: The receiver restarts into its out-of-box state and re-runs the setup assistant.

methods.description: Ethernet: plug into the NETWORK port and the receiver takes a DHCP lease with no menu interaction. This is the reliable option for a fixed installation — the Wi-Fi radio on this generation is 2.4/5 GHz 802.11n and the unit sits inside a metal chassis in a cabinet.
methods.name: Ethernet — plug in and take a DHCP lease

steps.action: Connect the NETWORK port to the LAN and power the receiver on.
steps.expect: Setup > Network shows an IP address; the Wi-Fi radio is disabled automatically when the cable is present.

steps.action: Setup > Network > Network Control > Always On (same reason as above).

methods.description: Wi-Fi join from the receiver's own setup menu: Setup > Network > Connection > Wi-Fi > Configuration, then pick the SSID and enter the passphrase with the remote. Two shortcuts exist on this generation — WPS push-button, and "Share Wi-Fi settings from an iOS device", which copies the credentials over the USB cable from a connected iPhone. The passphrase never crosses a link a third-party client could implement, which is why `credentials` records it as not applicable rather than plaintext.
methods.name: Wi-Fi from the receiver's on-screen setup menu

steps.action: Connect the receiver's MONITOR OUT to a TV so the setup GUI is visible.
steps.notes: The front-panel display can drive the same menus, but the on-screen GUI is far easier.

steps.action: Setup > Network > Connection > Wi-Fi, choose the SSID and enter the passphrase (or use WPS).
steps.expect: The Network menu shows the assigned IP address.

steps.action: Setup > Network > Network Control > Always On.
steps.notes: Without this the receiver answers nothing on the LAN while in standby, so a client can read state and control it only while somebody has already switched it on by hand.

steps.action: Confirm the goform surface answers from the LAN.
steps.expect: XML `<item>` document on port 80 carrying Power, InputFuncSelect, MasterVolume and Mute.

setup.notes: Onboarding happens on the receiver itself, through its setup menu shown on the connected TV (or on the front-panel display) — there is no app-driven provisioning protocol to reimplement, and the control surface needs no pairing once the unit is on the network. The step that matters for every consumer of this spec is not the network join but the one after it: Setup > Network > Network Control must be set to "Always On", or the receiver's entire LAN surface — HTTP, port 23, UPnP and mDNS alike — is powered down in standby, and no client can turn it back on. The trade-off is real and the user's to make: "Always On" raises idle power draw, and Denon ships it off on some model years.

rejoin.notes: Re-running Setup > Network > Connection changes the network without touching anything else, and it does not need the old network to still be up — the credentials are entered on the receiver, not handed to it by a client. Ethernet takes precedence over Wi-Fi automatically when a cable is present, so moving a Wi-Fi-provisioned unit onto a wired network needs no menu work at all.

steps.action: Setup > Network > Connection > Wi-Fi > Configuration, pick the new SSID, enter the passphrase.

testing.notes: The discovery half rests on a live LAN scan of a real AVR-S720W contributed 2026-08-23 (`evidence.live_lan_scan`): the mDNS service set, the AirPlay/RAOP and Spotify Connect TXT records, the SSDP notification types and the `KnOS/3.2 UPnP/1.0 DMP/3.5` SERVER string are quoted from it. Nothing in the control surface — goform, the ASCII command vocabulary, or UPnP — has been driven against hardware by this project; those facts are graded `reported` and come from Denon's published control-protocol documents and from open-source implementations (denonavr, the openHAB denonmarantz binding).

characteristics: The unit this spec was written against; scanned live 2026-08-23.
AirPlay TXT records report the model without the hyphen, as AVRS720W (`am` and `model`).
Default hostname Denon-AVR-S720W.local, until the owner renames the receiver.
Single zone — the Zone2/Zone3 status documents and the Z2/Z3 command prefixes do not apply.
AirPlay 1 only (srcvers 190.9.p6); no AirPlay 2, no HEOS Built-in, no HEOS CLI on port 1255.
variants.name: Denon AVR-S720W (2016, 7.2 ch)

characteristics: Same 2016 KnOS firmware generation and the same goform/telnet surface.
Whether this model exposes a second zone was not established here; probe /goform/formZone2_Zone2XmlStatusLite.xml rather than assuming.
variants.name: Denon AVR-S920W (2016, 7.2 ch)

characteristics: X-series sibling of the same generation; same control surface, richer setup menu.
variants.name: Denon AVR-X1300W (2016, 7.2 ch)

entities.name: Power
entities.notes: Discrete on and off, no toggle — the receiver has separate commands for both, so a bulk "everything off" is safe here. The control is only reachable at all when Setup > Network > Network Control is "Always On"; with it off the receiver is unreachable in standby and this switch can turn the unit off but never back on. A consumer that sees the address stop answering right after a successful turn_off should report that state rather than an error.

entities.name: Volume
entities.notes: Reported and set in the same units, so no conversion is needed on this route — but the reading is a STRING that is not always a number: `--` means minimum. Parse defensively and map it to -80. `max` here is the protocol ceiling, not a promise: the receiver's own configured maximum (`MVMAX`) is lower on most installations and clamps anything above it, and it is readable only on port 23. Over HTTP, expect a set above the ceiling to come back clamped in the next status read rather than as an error.

entities.name: Mute
entities.notes: The status document spells this lower case while the command spells it upper case; compare case-insensitively rather than matching `on_value` exactly, or the control reads as never engaged.

entities.name: Input
entities.notes: The static list is the family vocabulary and a fallback, not the truth for a given unit. The authoritative list is `<InputFuncList>` in `/goform/formMainZone_MainZoneXml.xml`, with user-facing labels positionally alongside it in `<RenameSource>`; a consumer that can fetch that document should replace these options with what it finds and show the renamed labels while sending the wire tokens. The options are not bound through `options_source` because that contract reads an attribute off each matched element, and this device puts the value in element text instead.

entities.name: Surround Mode
entities.notes:
Two things make this select unusual, and a consumer that models it as an ordinary one will misbehave on both.
First, the selection is a REQUEST: the receiver picks what the incoming stream allows and reports that instead, with no error. Show the value read back from `<SurrMode>`, never the value last sent.
Second — and following from it — THE STATE ROUTINELY FALLS OUTSIDE THE OPTIONS. `options` lists the modes that can be REQUESTED; `<SurrMode>` reports the mode in force, which is drawn from a wider set that names the decoder actually running (`DOLBY DIGITAL`, `DTS SURROUND`, `MULTI CH IN`, `STEREO`). A consumer must render an unlisted value as the current state rather than treating it as invalid or blanking the control; only the send side is restricted to `options`.
State comes from the full status document rather than the Lite one, which does not carry it — so this entity costs a second, heavier fetch and should not drive the poll interval.

not_decoded:
`ft`/`features` 0x444F8A00 is the AirPlay feature bitfield. It is recorded verbatim rather than decoded: the bit assignments come from reverse-engineered community tables that disagree with one another in places, and nothing in this spec depends on any individual bit.
`fv` p106348.1400.0 is a firmware/build string in D&M's own format. It is worth logging when reporting a bug against a unit, but this project has no map from it to a user-facing firmware version.
live_lan_scan.reading: What the scan settles, and what it does not. Settled: the unit is a D&M-firmware media renderer (`KnOS/`) whose model string is machine readable as `AVRS720W` in two independent places (`am` and `model`); it is an AirPlay 1 receiver and not an AirPlay 2 one (`srcvers`/`vs` 190.9.p6, and no `pk` public-key record — an AirPlay 2 speaker advertises one); RAOP will accept PCM and ALAC (`cn: 0,1`) over UDP (`tp`) with either no encryption or FairPlay (`et: 0,4`) and can show text, artwork and progress metadata (`md: 0,1,2`); and Spotify Connect is served from the same port 80 web server as the control API, under D&M's own `/goform/` namespace. Not settled by a scan: anything about the control surface. Every goform path, command spelling and status document below is graded `reported` from published documents and open-source implementations, not from this scan.

http_endpoints.description: The cheap state read, and the one to poll: power, selected input, volume-display preference, master volume and mute for the main zone. Use this rather than the full document for anything on a timer — the full one is several times the size and re-sends the input list on every poll.
http_endpoints.name: Main Zone Status (Lite)

fields.description: Selected input as a wire token (MPLAY, SAT/CBL, BD, TUNER, NET, BT, ...).
fields.name: InputFuncSelect.value

fields.description: Relative or Absolute — a front-panel display preference only; MasterVolume is reported in relative dB either way.
fields.name: VolumeDisplay.value

fields.description: Signed decimal dB relative to reference, roughly -80.0 to +18.0. The literal string `--` means minimum.
fields.name: MasterVolume.value

fields.description: on or off, lower case (the command spelling is upper case).
fields.name: Mute.value

http_endpoints.description: Everything the Lite document has, plus the facts a client needs ONCE per connection rather than on every poll: `<FriendlyName>` (what the owner named the receiver), `<Model>`, `<ZonePower>` (the main-zone power, as distinct from whole-unit power), `<SurrMode>` (the surround mode actually in force), `<InputFuncList>` — the inputs THIS unit accepts, which is the only authoritative source for populating an input picker — and `<RenameSource>`, the user-facing labels for those inputs. Fetch it when a device is first discovered and after the user changes something structural; poll the Lite document in between.
http_endpoints.name: Main Zone Status (Full)

fields.description: Owner-assigned display name, e.g. 'Denon AVR-S720W' out of the box.
fields.name: FriendlyName.value

fields.description: Model string as the receiver reports it.
fields.name: Model.value

fields.description: Main zone power (ASCII ZM): ON or OFF.
fields.name: ZonePower.value

fields.description: Surround mode in force — which may not be the one last requested; the receiver falls back based on the incoming stream.
fields.name: SurrMode.value

fields.description: Repeated <value> children, one per input this unit accepts. The authoritative per-unit list.
fields.name: InputFuncList.value

fields.description: Repeated <value> children positionally matching InputFuncList — the user-facing label for each input. A blank entry means the input was never renamed; fall back to the wire token.
fields.name: RenameSource.value

http_endpoints.description:
Now-playing for the built-in network sources (internet radio, DLNA, Spotify Connect, USB): track, artist, album and transport state. Only meaningful while the selected input is a network source; on any other input it answers with stale or empty fields rather than an error, so gate the read on `InputFuncSelect` rather than trusting the content.
No `response_body` fields, and deliberately no entity bound to it: this project has not established the element names inside the document, and an entity naming a path nobody has checked renders as a permanently blank tile. The endpoint is catalogued so an implementer knows where to look; binding a sensor to it is work for whoever reads one.
http_endpoints.name: Network Audio Status

http_endpoints.description: Band, frequency and preset for the built-in tuner. Meaningful only while the TUNER input is selected.
http_endpoints.name: Tuner Status

http_endpoints.description: A one-shot identity document — model name, MAC address, the number of zones the unit has, and a `CommApiVers` that tells a client which AppCommand envelope generation the receiver speaks. Where it answers it is the cleanest identity source on the device, which is why it is listed; it is marked unverified because its presence varies by firmware generation and this project has not confirmed it on an AVR-S720W. Treat a 404 as normal and fall back to `<Model>`/`<FriendlyName>` in the full status document, or to the UPnP description.
http_endpoints.name: Device Info

fields.description: The unit's MAC without separators; begins 0005CD on D&M hardware.
fields.name: Device_Info.MacAddress

fields.description: How many zones the receiver has — the reliable way to decide whether the Zone2/Zone3 endpoints are worth probing.
fields.name: Device_Info.DeviceZones

fields.description: Which AppCommand envelope generation the unit speaks; decides between AppCommand.xml and AppCommand0300.xml.
fields.name: Device_Info.CommApiVers

fields.description: Distinguishes the D&M brands (Denon, Marantz). The exact code-to-brand mapping is not established by this project — read it, log it, and do not branch behaviour on a guessed value.
fields.name: Device_Info.BrandCode

http_endpoints.description: The batched-query route: one POST carries several named queries and the reply carries their answers in the same order. Worth using in place of several status GETs when a client wants a specific handful of readings — it is one round trip against an HTTP server that does not like concurrency. The Lite status document remains the better choice for a plain poll.
http_endpoints.name: App Command

fields.description: One query name per <cmd> element, with an `id` attribute naming the envelope generation (1 for this route). Known names include GetAllZonePowerStatus, GetVolumeLevel, GetMuteStatus, GetSourceStatus, GetSurroundModeStatus, GetRenameSource, GetDeletedSource and GetZoneName.
fields.name: tx.cmd

fields.description: One <cmd> element per request element, in request order. Match by position; the reply does not echo the query name.
fields.name: rx.cmd

http_endpoints.description: The later envelope generation of the same route, with `id="3"` on each <cmd> and a wider query vocabulary. Newer receivers answer this one and may answer only this one; older firmware 404s it. Decide by `CommApiVers` from Device Info where that endpoint exists, otherwise try it once and fall back. Not established on an AVR-S720W.
http_endpoints.name: App Command (0300)

http_endpoints.description: The universal control route: `{command}` is one ASCII command from `protocol_details.denon_common.command_vocabulary`, sent exactly as it would go over port 23 and WITHOUT a terminator. Answers 200 with an empty or stub body whether or not the command was meaningful — the receiver does not report rejection here, so a client that needs to know whether a change took must re-read a status document. For the same reason the `?` QUERY FORMS ARE USELESS ON THIS ROUTE: the answer goes to the ASCII channel, not to the HTTP response, so it is lost. Percent-encode the space in the commands that carry one (`MSDOLBY%20DIGITAL`).
http_endpoints.name: Direct Command

http_endpoints.description: Power for one zone: `{zone}` is 1 for the main zone, `{state}` is `PowerOn` or `PowerStandby`. Equivalent to `PWON`/`PWSTANDBY` on the DIRECT route; this is the spelling the receiver's own web UI uses. The literal `+` is a plus in the bytes sent, not an encoded space.
http_endpoints.name: Set Power

http_endpoints.description:
Absolute volume for one zone, where `{level}` is the signed dB decimal the status documents report, not the offset integer the ASCII `MV` command wants. This asymmetry is the single easiest thing to get wrong on this device: the two encodings differ by 80 (dB = MV - 80), so a reading of `-20.0` is sent here as `-20.0` but on the DIRECT route as `MV60`. Confuse them and `MV20` arrives, which is -60 dB — 40 dB quiet; confuse them the other way and a `MV60` reading is shown as +60 dB.
NOTE FOR WHOEVER WRITES THE TEST: -40 dB is the one level where the two encodings share their digits (-40 dB is `MV40`), so a round-trip test at -40.0 passes through the wrong route and hides the bug. Test at -20.0.
Range roughly -80.0 to +18.0, in 0.5 dB steps.
http_endpoints.name: Set Volume

http_endpoints.description: Mute for one zone; `{state}` is `MuteOn` or `MuteOff`. Note the status document reports the same fact as lower-case `on`/`off`.
http_endpoints.name: Set Mute

http_endpoints.description: Spotify's zeroconf identity endpoint, whose path came from the `_spotify-connect._tcp` `cpath` TXT record. Returns JSON with the receiver's Spotify device id, name, public key and active user. Not part of Denon's control surface and not needed to drive the receiver — listed because a successful reply is the strongest single confirmation on the network that an unidentified host is a D&M device, and because it is how a client would hand the receiver a Spotify account.
http_endpoints.name: Spotify Connect Info

http_endpoints.description: The receiver's own browser control page, served from the same port. Of no use to a programmatic client — it is a frameset driving the same goform endpoints — but it is the right thing to deep-link a user to, and it is what `device.admin_url` points at.
http_endpoints.name: Web Control UI

absent_surfaces.description: What this generation does NOT have, recorded because a consumer that probes for it and finds nothing should not conclude the device is broken or unsupported.
absent_surfaces.heos_cli: No HEOS Built-in, so no HEOS CLI on TCP 1255. That interface arrived with the 2018 AVR-S750H and the X-series H models. On an AVR-S720W port 1255 is closed, and a closed 1255 is the expected result, not a fault. Network audio on this generation is driven through the goform surface and `/goform/formNetAudio_StatusXml.xml` instead.
absent_surfaces.websocket_or_push_over_http: None. HTTP state is polled, full stop; the only push is the port 23 session. A poll every 5-10 seconds while a UI is on screen, and rather less often otherwise, is what open-source implementations settle on.
absent_surfaces.zones: The AVR-S720W is single-zone. The `Zone2`/`Zone3` status documents and the `Z2`/`Z3` command prefixes belong to the family, not to this model; probing `/goform/formZone2_Zone2XmlStatusLite.xml` is how a consumer finds out for a given unit, and a 404 or an empty document is the answer.

command_vocabulary.description:
The ASCII command set, shared verbatim by port 23 and by the DIRECT HTTP route. Each command is the two-letter (occasionally three-letter) group followed by its argument, and appending `?` asks for the current value instead of setting one. On port 23 every command is terminated with a single CR (0x0D, no LF); on the DIRECT route the terminator is supplied by the receiver and must not be sent.
THE QUERY FORMS ARE A PORT 23 FEATURE. A `?` command sent over the DIRECT HTTP route is accepted, but its answer arrives on the ASCII channel, which that route does not expose — the HTTP response is the same empty stub every other DIRECT command gets, so the reading is simply lost. Over HTTP, read state from the status documents in `http_endpoints` instead. The `?` forms are documented because they are how a port 23 client reads state, and because a few facts (`MVMAX`) are reachable no other way.

groups.meaning: Master volume as an OFFSET INTEGER, not dB: dB = MV - 80, so 00 is minimum, 80 is the 0 dB reference and `MV50` is -30 dB. A third digit is a half step — `MV505` is -29.5 dB. `MVUP`/`MVDOWN` step by the receiver's own increment. `MV?` answers TWICE: the current level as `MVxx`, then the configured ceiling as `MVMAX xx`. Both lines start `MV`, so a client that matches on the prefix and keeps the last match reads the ceiling as the level. Take the first reply and treat `MVMAX` as a separate fact.

groups.notes: This is the family vocabulary, not a per-unit list: the sources an individual receiver accepts depend on its model and on which inputs the owner hid in the setup menu. The authoritative list for the unit in front of you is `<InputFuncList>` in `/goform/formMainZone_MainZoneXml.xml`; read it and offer that, rather than offering all of these and letting some silently do nothing.

Surround modes are gated by the incoming stream: asking for a multichannel mode on a two-channel source is accepted and ignored, and the receiver reports back whatever it actually selected. Always re-read `SurrMode` rather than assuming the request took.

groups.meaning: Parameter settings — tone controls, dynamic EQ, dialogue level and the rest of the audio-parameter menu (`PSBAS UP`, `PSTRE DOWN`, `PSDYNEQ ON`, ...). Catalogued here as a group rather than enumerated: the set is large, model-dependent, and this project has no evidence for which members the AVR-S720W accepts.

request_format.description:
Requests go to `http://<ip>/goform/<form>` with no headers of any kind required — no authentication, no Content-Type on the GET routes, no cookies, no session. Control GETs carry their whole instruction in the query string and answer with an empty or trivial body; state is read by GETting a status document and parsing the XML.
Two families of control GET exist and they overlap:

  * The DIRECT route, `/goform/formiPhoneAppDirect.xml?<CMD>`, where
    <CMD> is one ASCII command from the vocabulary in
    `command_vocabulary` below — exactly what port 23 takes. Anything
    the protocol can express goes through here.
  * The FORM route, `/goform/formiPhoneAppPower.xml`,
    `formiPhoneAppVolume.xml`, `formiPhoneAppMute.xml`, whose argument
    is `<zone>+<value>` — zone 1 is the main zone. Narrower, but it is
    the route the vendor's own web UI uses and it takes volume as a
    signed dB decimal rather than the offset integer the ASCII MV
    command wants.

Prefer the DIRECT route for anything the FORM route does not cover, and note that the `+` in a FORM-route query string is a literal plus in the bytes that go out, not a percent-encoded space.
request_format.escaping:
The vocabulary is upper-case letters, digits, `/` and space. A space DOES appear in several commands (`MSMCH STEREO`, `MSPURE DIRECT`, `MSDOLBY DIGITAL`); on the DIRECT route it must be percent-encoded as `%20`, and the `/` in `SISAT/CBL` may be sent literally or as `%2F`.
This spec keeps command `parameters` in their RAW form — `MCH STEREO`, not `MCH%20STEREO` — because percent-encoding is the URL builder's job, not the value's, and because the raw token is also what the status documents report back, so one spelling serves both the send and the state match. A renderer substitutes the raw value into `path` and encodes as it builds the request line.
Commands are case-sensitive: `PWON` works, `pwon` does not.

http.body: Empty for every GET route; an XML document for the AppCommand POST route.
http.headers: None required. The receiver's HTTP server is minimal and old: it serialises requests, so a client that fires several at once can see timeouts or resets that look like the device being offline. Send sequentially, allow a generous timeout (several seconds), and retry once before declaring the unit unreachable.

response_format.description:
Control GETs answer 200 with an empty body or a stub XML document; the body is an acknowledgement that the request was accepted, NOT the resulting state. A client that needs to show the new state must re-read a status document — and should allow a beat before doing so, because the receiver applies input and surround changes asynchronously and will briefly report the old value.
Status documents are XML with no namespace, rooted at `<item>`, and almost every reading is wrapped one level deeper in a `<value>` child:

  <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
  <item>
    <Power><value>ON</value></Power>
    <InputFuncSelect><value>MPLAY</value></InputFuncSelect>
    <VolumeDisplay><value>Relative</value></VolumeDisplay>
    <MasterVolume><value>-40.0</value></MasterVolume>
    <Mute><value>off</value></Mute>
  </item>

The dotted paths this spec uses in `entities[].state_mapping` are resolved FROM THAT ROOT, not including it: `MasterVolume.value` names the text of the `<value>` element inside `<MasterVolume>`, exactly as wemo's `BinaryState` names an element inside its SOAP reply rather than the envelope path down to it. They are element paths, not JSON paths — the same dotted notation the rest of the catalogue uses for JSON replies, applied to XML because this device's replies are XML.

value_conventions.input: A short upper-case token (`MPLAY`, `SAT/CBL`, `BD`, `TUNER`, `NET`, `BT`, ...). It is the wire value, not a label: the user-facing name may have been renamed on the receiver, and the renamed labels are in `<RenameSource>` in the non-Lite status document. Render the rename when you have it, but send the wire value.
value_conventions.master_volume: A signed decimal in dB relative to reference, e.g. `-40.0`, spanning roughly -80.0 (minimum) to +18.0 (maximum). Two traps. First, at the very bottom the receiver reports the literal string `--` instead of a number; treat that as the minimum, not as a parse failure. Second, `VolumeDisplay` (`Relative` or `Absolute`) changes only what the FRONT PANEL prints — `MasterVolume` is reported in relative dB either way, so a client must not add 80 to it just because the panel is set to Absolute.
value_conventions.mute: `on` or `off`, LOWER case in the status documents, while the ASCII command spelling is upper case (`MUON`/`MUOFF`). Compare case-insensitively; the mismatch is a real source of "mute never reads as engaged" bugs.
value_conventions.power: `ON` or `STANDBY`, upper case. Note that `Power` and `ZonePower` are different questions: `Power` (ASCII `PW`) is the whole unit, and `STANDBY` there means the LAN surface is only answering at all because Network Control is "Always On". `ZonePower` (ASCII `ZM`) is the main zone, which on a multi-zone receiver can be off while the unit is on. On the single-zone AVR-S720W the two move together.

airplay.generation: AirPlay 1 (RAOP). srcvers/vs 190.9.p6 on the observed unit.
airplay.notes: No `pk` (public key) TXT record is advertised, which is the marker an AirPlay 2 receiver carries; senders that speak only AirPlay 2 will not see this receiver as a target at all. `et: 0,4` says it accepts both unencrypted and FairPlay-encrypted sessions, and `cn: 0,1` says PCM and ALAC, so an open-source sender has a workable path.
airplay.port: From the `_raop._tcp` SRV record — do not assume 5000/7000.

streaming_sinks.description: Two streaming receivers share the same address, and both are somebody else's protocol rather than Denon's. They are documented here for identification and for knowing what a user can already do, not as control surfaces.

spotify_connect.notes: The standard Spotify zeroconf handshake: `GET <cpath>?action=getInfo` returns the device's JSON identity and public key, and a `POST` with `action=addUser` plus an encrypted credential blob hands the receiver a Spotify account to stream with. This is Spotify's protocol, needs a Premium account, and can be withdrawn by Spotify independently of anything Denon does — treat it as out of scope for local control and useful mainly as the identification signal it is.
spotify_connect.zeroconf_path: /goform/spotifyConfig — from the `cpath` TXT record; served by the same port 80 web server as the control API.

telnet.description: Port 23, raw ASCII, CR-terminated. It is not a login shell — there is no banner, no prompt and no authentication; the socket opens and the receiver starts talking. It carries exactly the vocabulary above, and it is the ONLY surface that reports state changes without being asked: turn the volume knob on the front panel and a connected client sees `MV45` arrive unsolicited.
telnet.line_ending: CR (0x0D) only — no LF. A client that sends CRLF may see the LF treated as a second, empty command.
telnet.pacing: Commands need a gap between them — the widely used figure in open-source implementations is on the order of 100 ms. Sending a burst back to back gets some of them dropped with no error anywhere.
telnet.single_session: The receiver accepts ONE connection on port 23 at a time. A second client is refused or silently starved, and holding the socket locks out the vendor's own app and every other integration on the network. A consumer that opens it must close it promptly, must not hold it open as an idle keep-alive across a whole session, and should treat a connection refusal as "somebody else has it" rather than as the device being down.
telnet.why_http_instead: Because the vocabulary is identical, every entity in this spec binds to the HTTP route: a consumer loses nothing but the push, and gains the ability to coexist with whatever else on the network wants the single telnet session. Reach for port 23 only when unsolicited state updates are genuinely needed.

upnp.control_urls: Resolve them from `<serviceList>` in the description document the SSDP LOCATION header points at. They are not fixed across firmware generations and must not be hardcoded.
upnp.description: A standard UPnP MediaRenderer, advertised as `urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:MediaRenderer:1` with RenderingControl, ConnectionManager and AVTransport. Do NOT route power, volume, input or surround through it — goform is simpler, covers all four, and does not require resolving a control URL first. What UPnP gives you that goform cannot is the opposite direction: `AVTransport::SetAVTransportURI` followed by `Play` hands the receiver a media URL to fetch and play by itself, which is the one thing the control API has no verb for.
upnp.server_header: KnOS/3.2 UPnP/1.0 DMP/3.5 — observed live; `KnOS/` is the D&M firmware platform.
